title: 3 gym etiquette faux pas (don't step over that barbell!)
summary: 100-subscriber special in which NH lists three gym etiquette mistakes: stepping over someone else's barbell, refusing to let people work in on shared equipment, and talking to people who wear headphones or are mid-set. He frames the gym as a shared community and the chatty gym guy as a drain on focus and rest.

claims.claim: Never step over someone else's barbell; walk around it. Where NH comes from this is seen as an insult or aggression and people will confront you over it.
NH finds stepping over barbells common in his current gyms and suspects it is a piece of older lifting culture that has been lost.
A gym is a community, not your personal property: if someone asks to work in with you, be reasonable and let them.

Refusing to share is understandable on barbell lifts where the other person would change your squat/bench height or strip heavy deadlift plates, but on machines and stations changing the weight costs nothing, so let people in.
Being refused a work-in leaves you standing around waiting, and some people even assume you are trying to intimidate them into giving up the equipment.
If someone has headphones in, don't keep talking to them; a wave or handshake is fine. This applies outside the gym too.
People have stepped into NH's field of vision to talk to him mid-set during squats and overhead press, which he finds absurd.
The guy who won't leave you alone at the gym costs you gains: he slows your workout, kills your focus and disrupts your rest times; tell him to go away despite disliking confrontation.
